title: Same-Visit Low-Use Allowance: Workmanship Warranties Training Questions
content:
Under the Workmanship Warranties, a same-visit low-use allowance is added into the same-visit courtesy sum on a Collision Lifetime Workmanship Warranty or Certified Structural Lifetime Warranty. The same-visit low-use allowance follows the miles driven from the odometer at issue to the odometer recorded at the coverage's most recent concern report: fewer than the low-use miles of 30000, the low-use courtesy allowance of USD 2.00; 30000 or more but fewer than the moderate-use miles of 60000, the moderate-use courtesy allowance of USD 1.00; 60000 or more, no same-visit low-use allowance.

## Training questions

Q. Which odometer readings are compared?
A. The odometer at issue recorded on the coverage, and the odometer recorded on the coverage's most recent concern report, whatever kind of concern that report was.

Q. What does each band give?

| Miles driven since issue | Same-visit low-use allowance |
|---|---|
| fewer than 30000 | USD 2.00 |
| 30000 to 59999 | USD 1.00 |
| 60000 or more | none |

Q. Where exactly do the bands change?
A. At 30000 miles driven the allowance falls from USD 2.00 to USD 1.00; at 60000 miles driven it falls to none. A hypothetical coverage issued at 18000 miles with a latest report at 47999 miles has driven 29999 miles: USD 2.00. At 48000 miles reported it has driven 30000: USD 1.00.
